title: The Teahouse on the Pass
status: complete; rebuild and content verification passed

planned.paragraphMeaning: Mio and Sōta travel from town toward the north mountain pass, pushing their bicycles up the steep road through the cool cedar woods after riding between the rice fields.
planned.sceneDescription: Two Japanese children push their bicycles uphill along a quiet mountain road where the rice fields give way to cedar forest; the pass rises ahead under a bright blue sky with distant white summer thunderclouds.

planned.paragraphMeaning: At the old teahouse on the pass, Mio tells the white-bearded owner her name; he stops fanning himself and recognises her as Takagi’s granddaughter.
planned.sceneDescription: At a small wooden Japanese mountain teahouse, white-bearded Gen-san sits on the front bench with his fan paused as Mio and Sōta arrive with their bicycles; the shop sign is present but blank and unreadable.

planned.paragraphMeaning: A sudden summer storm traps Mio and Sōta at the teahouse; Gen-san lets them inside and points out the old telephone so they can call home later.
planned.sceneDescription: Inside the quiet old teahouse, Mio and Sōta sit safely by a window while rain veils the cedar trees; Gen-san gestures toward a simple old corded telephone. No stranger has arrived yet.
